title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. These are notes for the 1976 IHES talk on the divided-power de Rham complex. The previous page sets up functors on cosimplicial (or simplicial) k-modules M_*: F_{Δ^n_*}(M_*) = M_[n] and K(M_*) = Ker(M_[1] ⇉ M_[0]). These carry 'multiplicative' structures F(M)⊗F(N) → F(M⊗N), modelled on the cochain algebra Ψ_* = k^{Δ^•} (so F_{Δ^n}(Ψ_*) = Ψ_[n] = k^{Δ^n}). The present page asks how much of a simplicial set X_* is remembered by its associated multiplicative functor F_{X_*}. It has three parts.

(1) Boxed lemma: independence of characters. Take ring maps u_i : A → B, with B (or the target field K ⊂ K') an integral domain; the note reads 'intègre'. Suppose Σ λ_i u_i = 0. Factor through k[T] → B, T ↦ b_i, so T^n ↦ b_i^n. Then Σ λ_i u_i(x)^n = 0 for all n. A Vandermonde argument then forces the λ's attached to each distinct value u_i(x) to sum to zero. The kernels Ker u_i = p_i are prime. Choosing t in the complement of ∪ p_i (= ∩ of the complements) and looking at differences u_i(x) − u_j(y) separates the distinct u_i. This is Dedekind–Artin linear independence of distinct multiplicative maps into a domain. The geometric gloss 'Y ← X_K' records the same thing as points of Spec.

(2) Main claim. Hom(Δ^m_*, Δ^n_*) ≅ Hom_mult(F_{Δ^n_*}, F_{Δ^m_*}): multiplicative natural transformations M_[n] → M_[m] are exactly those induced by simplicial maps. For a general X_* he defines X̃_* : n ↦ Hom_mult(F_{X_*}, F_{Δ^n_*}), with a canonical map X_* → X̃_*. Writing F_X = lim over Δ^m → X of F_{Δ^m}, he gets the chain
Hom(lim F_{Δ^m}, F_{Δ^n}) ← colim_{Δ^m/X} Hom(F_{Δ^m}, F_{Δ^n}) (marked 'iso?')
≅ colim Hom(Δ^n, Δ^m) = colim Δ^m_[n] ≅ X_[n].
So X_* ≅ X̃_* holds provided the 'iso?' step holds: a multiplicative map out of a limit must factor through some stage. This is a Tannakian / Gelfand-type reconstruction of a simplicial set from its multiplicative cochain functor.

(3) Bottom of page: attempt to justify 'iso?'. Given a multiplicative map ∏F_i → F_{Δ_n} (analogously ∏G_i → G_[n] or Ψ_[n]), he wants it to factor as u_i ∘ m_i through a single projection m_i. He tests this functorially in M_*, passing to Sym G(M_*) → Sym F(M_*) to turn multiplicative maps into ring maps so the boxed lemma applies. The lemma rules out non-trivial linear combinations Σλ_i u_i (crossed out), giving the factorization.
errors: The 'iso?' step is left open on the page. Commuting Hom out of an inverse limit with a colimit needs a finiteness or connectedness argument; for infinite X_n the product ∏ k is not the coproduct, and multiplicative maps from infinite products to a domain can fail to factor through a projection without finiteness or other hypotheses.
Dedekind independence needs the target to be a domain, or at least connected; this is noted ('intègre') but the reduction of functorial multiplicative maps to ring maps via Sym is only sketched.
The prime-avoidance step (t outside ∪ p_i) is only valid for finitely many p_i; this is implicit.

ideas.what: Linear independence of distinct multiplicative maps into an integral domain, via powers and Vandermonde
Simplicial maps Δ^m→Δ^n correspond bijectively to multiplicative natural transformations F_{Δ^n} → F_{Δ^m} between functors on cosimplicial modules
ideas.modern_name: Yoneda / Tannakian reconstruction of the simplex category from cochain algebras
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; cf. Toën (affine stacks), Mandell (cochains determine homotopy type) for homotopical versions
ideas.where_published: related 'schematization' ideas in Pursuing Stacks (1983) and letters

ideas.what: Recovering a simplicial set X as n ↦ Hom_mult(F_X, F_{Δ^n}), i.e. double-dual reconstruction from the multiplicative cochain functor
ideas.modern_name: Reconstruction of spaces from cochain (E∞ / cosimplicial) algebras; schematization

missed.claim: Around 1975-76, inside the divided-power de Rham project, Grothendieck sketches an exact (non-homotopical) reconstruction of a simplicial set from its multiplicative functor of 'cochains with coefficients in cosimplicial modules'. This is a precursor of the schematization / affine-stacks circle later made precise by Toën, and parallels Mandell's cochain-reconstruction theorems.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It shows the schematization idea, usually dated to Pursuing Stacks (1983), was already present in 1976 in connection with divided-power (crystalline-type) de Rham complexes. This is a historical link between crystalline cochains and algebraic models of homotopy types.

missed.claim: The key step, that multiplicative maps out of lim F_{Δ^m} factor through a stage, is left as 'iso?'. Only a sketch via Dedekind independence and Sym is given.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is minor; the exact-level statement is likely easy for finite simplicial sets but delicate in general.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean but elementary reconstruction argument. Its interest is mainly historical: an early appearance of reconstruction of simplicial sets from multiplicative cochain functors, tied to the divided-power de Rham work.
transcription_corrections: 'Ker u_i = 𝔭_i' with 'idéaux premiers' is correct; the annotation next to the commutative square reads '(K ou B) intègre', not 'i intègre'.
'Y ← X_r' is likely 'Y ← X_K' (points over a field K).
'Soit [-doux?-] Γ' is likely 'Soient ...' with a crossed-out word; the 'Γ' mark is probably a ditto mark over ∏.
'ℂ_[n]' is likely 'G_[n]' or 'Ψ_[n]', not complex numbers.
'Hom(Δ^n_*, Δ^m_*) ≃ Δ^m_[n]' is consistent with the image.
